statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ has now traded on both sides of its prior close since the futures restart, which is direct evidence that retracement is available, so Tail sits near its floor while Stress stays elevated on an unresolved crude supply premium and a 10-year yield near multi-year highs.
recommendation: Path risk across this window is concentrated in the 13:30Z-14:30Z US cash reopen, the first full-depth session to price three days of geopolitical and macro news at once. Outside that window the mapped state remains green with Tail well below the block threshold.
headline: NQ round-trips from +22 to -18 in the post-holiday reopen, and a two-sided path keeps Tail at 8 while crude near $93 and a 4.79% 10-year hold Stress at 63
body:
The most useful new observation of this run is not the level but the shape. An hour ago NQ printed 29,587.50, up 22.25 on the 29,565.25 prior close; it now prints 29,547.75, down 17.50 (-0.06%), corroborated to the tick by an independent quote at 19:15 ET. Price has therefore crossed the prior close in both directions inside the first ninety minutes of the Tuesday trade date. That is the opposite of the persistent one-way structure that defines a genuine tail path, and it is why Tail falls to 8 rather than rising on the weaker headline print. ES is the mild counter-signal at 7,703.50, down 18.50 (-0.24%) and sitting closer to its session low than NQ is to its own, so the two indices are not aligned; under the standing convention conflicting cross-checks raise uncertainty rather than Tail. Depth is still the thinnest of the week after the Labor Day halt, which caps both directional efficiency and conviction.

The background is genuinely stressed, and that is where the elevated Stress reading comes from rather than from anything in the current price path. WTI settled at $92.63, up 1.26% on a $90.87-$93.29 range, with Brent at $97.31 after touching a six-week high of $98.06. The driver is a step change in the US-Iran conflict: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday including one off Kharg Island, the IRGC claimed reciprocal strikes on three tankers and three US-linked vessels, and Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery was reported hit on Monday for the second time in a month. Commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz have averaged roughly ten ships a day over the past ten days, the lowest since May, and Goldman Sachs has flagged $120 crude if shipping attacks intensify. Layered on top, the 10-year Treasury yield stands near 4.79% and the 2-year near 4.37%, close to the highest levels since late 2023, after Friday's August payrolls came in at 162,000 against roughly 53,000-56,000 expected with unemployment steady at 4.1%. Futures now imply roughly a 60% chance of a quarter-point increase at the September 15-16 meeting.

Under the standing convention, event importance, surprise magnitude and hypothetical post-event chains inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail until observed price-path evidence establishes persistent mean-reversion failure. Nothing in the current tape does. Latest-session internals reinforce the dispersion reading rather than an aligned one: semiconductors were uniformly bid, with Micron up 6.1%, AMD 4.69%, Intel 4.51% and Arm 3.92%, while Apple fell 2.51%, Microsoft 2.04% and Tesla 5.92%. Strong rotation with a wide internal split is a mixed regime, not a directional one, and it is the basis for the mixed dominant mode this hour.

The forecast keeps path risk low through the Asian session, lifts it modestly at the 07:00Z European cash open, which is the first deep non-US repricing of the weekend escalation, and concentrates it at the 13:30Z US cash reopen. That reopen is the one genuine risk of the window because the tanker strikes, the refinery attack and the payrolls surprise all price at full depth simultaneously for the first time. The 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots alone map to WATCH, and the mapped danger window is 13:30Z-14:30Z. Tail is then projected to decay through the US afternoon on the assumption that price discovery proves orderly and retracements appear, with a modest nudge into the closing hour. Confidence at 79 reflects live corroborated NQ and ES quotes from two independent sources, oil from two sources, yields from two sources and verified geopolitical reporting; it is held below the very-high band because the VIX reading of 15.30 is Friday's close with US cash shut on Monday, and because the shared cross-asset context file was collected slightly outside its freshness window.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail confined to a 5-10% band, so no slot came close to the block threshold. Stress ran at 54-56% through the Asian and European sessions, stepped up to 61-64% across the US afternoon as crude extended into the holiday close, and held at 62-63% from the 17:00Z futures halt through the 22:00Z restart. Confidence sat at 85-86% while live price evidence was continuous, fell to 75-76% once the halt removed it, and has recovered as the restart became observable. Dominant mode was normal in twenty slots and mixed at 14:00Z, 16:00Z, 17:00Z and 22:00Z, where the energy-versus-equity divergence was widest.
outlookSummary: The reopen that the prior window flagged has now resolved benignly and then some: NQ traded above and below its prior close inside ninety minutes, so the opening slot carries observed two-way structure rather than a hypothesis, and Tail sits at 8. Path risk stays near the floor through the Asian session, rises modestly at the 07:00Z European cash open as the weekend tanker strikes and the Jazan refinery attack are repriced at real depth for the first time, and peaks at the 13:30Z US cash reopen. That reopen is the single concentrated risk of the window because three days of geopolitical and macro news, including Friday's 162,000-payroll surprise, price simultaneously at full depth; the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots alone map to WATCH and the mapped danger window is 13:30Z-14:30Z. Tail is then projected to decay through the US afternoon on the assumption of orderly price discovery with retracements present, with a modest nudge into the 19:00Z closing hour before returning to the overnight floor. Stress stays in the elevated band throughout because the crude supply premium and a 10-year yield near 4.79% are unresolved rather than because index structure is deteriorating.
